Stomp Rocket Original Stunt Plane Refill - 1 Looper Plane Only - Performs Giant Loop - Gift for Boys or Girls Age 5+ Years Old - Active STEM Play Per my 6 year old: He loves his Stomp Rocket Stunt Planes because of being able to run, jump, and stomp on it. He also LOVES the green plane.

Per this mama: I bought this on Prime Day for a birthday gift for my son. I thought being able to run and jump for hours only to see a rocket pop up in the air would be worth every penny. Turns out I was right. The only downside is that I would not use this if you have small backyard. I live in the city, but I have fairly large yard. The rockets fly all over the place because they are stunt planes as opposed to rockets that are supposed to pop straight up into the sky. Think of the Stomp Rocket like a sewing machine. There's a pedal that you "stomp" to make the rocket go. Instead of electricity, air in the pedal flows into a tube and propels the rocket outward. The harder you stomp the higher it goes. The softer, then it doesn't go very far.

All of the planes are shaped differently and they each do different tricks. We haven't figured out all the best angles yet, but my son loves watching them go and then he runs after them. I would rather have just rockets because I hate having to traverse the poison ivy hill on the outskirts of my lawn, but you know whatever keeps the kids happy.

text_fidelity_a:
Happy The Birthday Bird Stuffed Plush Animal with Interactive Book – Adorable Book Character Stuffed Animals with Birthday Theme - Soft Cuddly Fabric – Includes Memory Pages, Photo Storing Pocket I have had several friends who have given birth over the last year or so. Many of them have had all sorts of great ideas and things happen. When I saw this set, I knew one in particular had to have it.

WHAT THIS IS LIKE
This is in a really cool gift box as shown in the promo from the company. It is a clear front and the bird, balloon, and book are visible through the window. There is a ribbon handle at the top.

HOW THIS WORKS
This works so that you have the little doll, put the balloon on the doll which goes with the story. You hide a little gift in the bird and the child can have fun looking for it. The book allows you to document this journey every year.

BACK POCKET
The book has a back pocket so that you can put the picture in the book of that year. When the new year comes out, you repeat the journey and then take off the older picture, put it in the back pocket, and then put the newest picture documenting the even in its place.

HOW DO THEY LIKE THIS?
This was so well received. The bird is adorable. There are sparkles in his eyes, the sneakers are red metallic, and the design is appealing and really cute. The little backpack allows for a small gift, but nothing large. This is just what this particular family needed. They wanted to document their baby's growth and have a really alert a curious little one who loves things like this.

ADOPTION
If you happen to be someone who is involved in adoption, this also might be a great way for the open adoption to share the growth of the baby with the birth mom or family. It would be a great bridge between the mom and dear family who adopts the children.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I highly recommend this set. If you have a child age 2 or so you can start the tradition. You can start as a baby, but with restrictions on the journey. It is a really cool tradition to encourage kids to be who they are meant to be, have fun documenting the tradition and keep track of their growth for future reference as a family keep sake.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is endearing and I will be buying more of these for other families that I know who would love it.
text_fidelity_b: Happy The Birthday Bird Stuffed Plush Animal with Interactive Book – Adorable Book Character Stuffed Animals with Birthday Theme - Soft Cuddly Fabric – Includes Memory Pages, Photo Storing Pocket

Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink This convertible car for 14 inch dolls is completely awesome. We have a number of glitter girls dolls and two of them can fit into this convertible with ease, along with one of the glitter girls puppies sitting on a lap.

My kids saw this in a Christmas catalog and were completely enchanted with it, asking for it over and over again. It's about as big as you would expect given that the glitter girls both have to fit in there, and it has a dashboard that opens, a little side container that opens in between the two seats, two cupholders, and the trunk.

We have the glitter girls sweetshop and the accessories sweetshop that has some delightful cups of confectionery beverage, and I was delighted to find that these sweetshop beverages fit into the cupholders perfectly. (They also fit into the girls hands). The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. Same thing with the little container in between the two seats, if that could have been just a little bit wider, it would get used even more.

The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.

Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions I am always looking for fun games that my family and I can enjoy together on game night and having not heard of Selfie I decided to give it a shot. It is a fun game but seems based on some other popular games that have been around for a while.

“Selfie” could just have easily been called “Apples to Apples Meets Charades!” which is a fairly concise way to describe it. Each player is dealt a set of cards describing a scenario where one would make some kind of facial expression, and then takes a selfie shot of that expression. After looking at the selfie shot, everyone else then plays one of their own cards to describe the expression, from which the original player selects a winner he/she likes most. Each person takes a turn taking a selfie and selecting others’ cards.

The game can be played without a phone or camera but it’s a lot easier with such a device which will help eliminate disagreements.

It should be obvious that this is not a game for the self-conscious individual.

Though I don’t think this game is all that original, it is a fun game and works in a crowd. This is the kind of game to break out during a party in the dorms or on a Saturday night with the family. It’s fun, gameplay is lively and fast-paced.
text_fidelity_b: Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions

Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart This CRAFT-TASTIC 3D STRING ART KIT provides an inexpensive (about $6.25 on Amazon) introduction to the string art craft. It includes a snap-together plastic frame, plenty of colored embroidery floss for string, and reasonably clear instructions. The box says it's for ages 8 and up, which seems about right. (Adult help might be needed to assemble the frame, which requires the pegs to be properly oriented upwards or downwards for everything to snap together tightly.)

There is some artistic creativity involved with this kit, as there are no stringing diagrams to follow. Instead, the instructions say to knot your string to a peg in the frame, and then "wrap the thread from a peg in one (upper) heart to a peg on the other side (the lower heart)." This is simple enough, but it's up to you to choose the pegs so that you get an eye-pleasing criss-crossing of the thread.

Personally, I don't care for the color combinations: bright blue small inside heart, purple edge for the large outside heart, yellow front of large outside heart, pink back of large outside heart. When you're finished with all the stringing, you can set the big heart up on a little plastic stand.

A small child might enjoy this project a lot. However, being an adult, I was bored by the time I'd finished the small blue heart. Because this kit persuaded me that I don't care for the string art craft, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale). However, the budget price probably makes it a reasonable purchase if the intent is to keep a small child busy.
text_fidelity_b: Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes One 3D String Art Heart

Large 2.5LB Professional Rock Tumbler Kit, 3-Speed Motor & 9-Day Timer, Rubber Barrel, Quiet Rotary Stone Polisher with 5 Belts, Rough Gemstones, 4 Polishing Grits, for Adults Kids (Black) My kids have recently shown interest in gems and geology, so they were super excited to try this out! This is a full kit, which means it comes with everything you need: Not only the tumbler parts, but also the various stage mixes and even the raw rocks to use!
I actually was hoping it was the sort of thing we could use more than once, learn how to use it with the included stuff and then do more of our own found rocks with the next batch! The thing is, it comes with only enough to do the included rocks, and you have to do them all at once if you want them to come out with the included materials. Beyond that, you can reuse the machine but you have to get more materials to put in with the rocks.
The machine also takes a LONG time. I knew tumbling was a process, but it's a few stages and each one takes a few days, so the whole thing took weeks of emptying out and putting in the next stage and setting the timer for the next set of days spinning. The entire process from start to finish was nearly a month. But, my kids loved it and it was a very educational experience. I wish it came with more DIY material, but I guess I'll have to find some more to do our own ones next!

The biggest problem is that the pieces do not have consistent tolerances for the connecting portions. Sometimes they snap together easily while other times it takes a lot of force. Last, it would have been nice to have a couple of example layouts included in the instructions. This is not too big of a deal, but the pieces are difficult to connect and take apart, so for my kids’ sake, knowing some layouts that use the different sections properly would be nice.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy The Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is an educational toy in the shape of a clock, made from wood, with small wooden sorting blocks that fit into designated spaces. This toy helps to teach kids how to tell time and match shapes and it makes a great toy option for youngsters in the preschool age group.

Educational toys are the preferred toy from a parental point of view, but it is sometimes a challenge to find an educational toy that my girls will enjoy for an extended period of time. With the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock, it appears I have achieved victory in this area. Even weeks after their initial encounter with this toy, my girls still enjoying sorting the blocks and reading the numbers on the clock dial. Each of the blocks is colored differently and shaped differently and my girls enjoying figuring out which block fits into which slot.

One of the many advantages with the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is its ability to educate in multiple ways. Not only does it teach kids spatial skills and how to tell time, it also teaches kids how to match numbers, count the minutes and hours, and arrange the hands of the clock to a certain time. With the blocks, younger children will have two ways to match: By shape or by number. If they cannot match the number, they can match the shape that fits, thus eliminating frustration and eventually learning the number in the process. Yet another advantage of this toy is that it encourages more imaginative play. There are no bells or whistles and no batteries. The hands of the clock are moved only by pushing with the fingers. These facts make the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock a little on the old- fashioned side, in a sense, but in a positive way.

Educational toys are the best but it is often a challenge to find an educational toy that children will enjoy. This toy has passed the test with flying colors, offering satisfaction to both child and parent. It is true that the small blocks can get lost in due time, but other than this, the Melissa and Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock is an excellent toy overall. It teaches children several skills and offers great durability, is made from wood, and requires no batteries. My little ones love it and continue to enjoy it day after day. It's an easy winner that belongs in every child's toy box.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Wooden Shape Sorting Clock Educational Toy

I wasn't sure what to expect based on the box and description, but unlike other contraption based games I've played (like the classic "mouse trap" from my youth), this is more of a cooperative play game.
There are 4 strings that move a (clearly mission-impossible inspired) suspended character around the playing board, and it takes careful pulling and releasing each of them as a group effort to navigate properly, sort of like a marionette puppet meets a corporate team building activity. There are some things to do like remove security cameras and traps but the truth is, the real fun doesn't start until you open up the jewel cage.
Once the cage is open, there's a countdown (you can hear the spring noise whirring as soon as it opens) and the police car starts to slowly circle the board. If you make it to the getaway car with the jewel before the car makes it to block your path, you win! If, however, you take too long, the police car will spring into place and block your path. Hilarity ensues as players start to panic and lose their cool, and in the end, whether you make it or not, it felt exciting.
Things I like about the game:
- It is cooperative, not individual. So you don't "beat" another player, you work as a team to complete the task in time.
- The mechanical game board is unique and really fun to learn
- It does NOT require batteries! The board uses spring loaded timers where necessary, no electricity. This is cool in a decidedly analog way.
- People can walk over and see how it is played and join with very little instruction

Things I did not, however, like:
- The truth is, when playing with my kids, we sort of skipped the first part of the game and just jumped to the jewel part. The designers of this game tried to make it longer by adding disarming traps and pulling security cameras in particular order based on cards, but it felt tedious after a few rounds. Really the fun part is the end. The whirring police car gives a sense of danger and urgency that makes it fun.
- That little spy is suspended by strings that get tangled so quickly and easily. It feels like I sneeze and they are tangled. Out of the box, I had to spend time untwisting it before we played for the first time, so be careful.

That being said, the game is TON of fun for different ages and we actually had some guests come over who looked at it and wanted to play too (adults AND kids). They all asked where to to get it, so it might become a regular thing found in our neighborhood. I'd say it deserves 5 stars, it's been a while since a game sparked this much interest that wasn't on a screen.
text_fidelity_b: Moose Racing Mission: Diamond Heist Game Board with Spy, Challenges and Instructions, Multi (91009)

Granted my kid's only 7, and this is for 14+ (which at this point I agree 100% with). I'm not going to knock a star for that, mine is young and it was a risk he wanted to take. He often does the 14+ lego sets so I figured we'd be fine. NOPE. NO SIR. NOT TODAY.

There were so many tiny pieces, like unnecessarily tiny. He made it to step 2 and couldn't make heads or tails of the instructions. I took a look and also struggled which meant he felt vindicated and took off. So, I spent the next 2 hours debating life choices and contemplating day drinking. Ugh parenting is hard sometimes.

Be very aware: This is not a lego set. The pieces do not snap together as well, or stay together as well, there are no extra pieces, and the instructions are frustrating. I'm keeping my language clean here, but imagine a much more colorful word than frustrating. "Frustrating" really doesn't do the whole experience justice.

However, Boris is built. It can be done. PERSEVERANCE PEOPLE. Kiddo however is not allowed to touch it. It will go up on his bookshelf, like super high and when ever anyone walks in he is to loudly proclaim MY MOM BUILT THAT!

....on the upside it's priced pretty cheap, so if you have any kids in your life whose parents you want to torture, send this to them as a gift. So in the end I'm giving this 3 stars. One star off for the less then stellar pieces, and another star off for the horrendous instructions.
text_fidelity_b: Bendy and the Ink Machine - Boris Buildable Figure (202 pieces), 60 months to 180 months

However, despite all of that the item is sturdy, looks good, and rides well. I put the seat on the last holes for my 5 year old (almost 6) who is 4' tall and it works well for him. I like that the rules are pretty easy and it works a little like tetris as you try to cover space and penalty areas with rocks while protecting bonus areas with trees. TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+ When I was in high school my senior class played an elimination game that was vaguely similar to this (and has been around for years and is still played across the country). Each person drew a name and that was the "target", and there were only loose rules on how to "eliminate" your target (most memorable weapon was a seltzer bottle), and graduation was the time limit. TAG is basically a formalization of that game, with fewer players and more specifics on elimination.

My graduating class had over 500 people, and not all of them played the game. Still, with 50+ players and months to play, it was unwieldy then. TAG limits the game to 10 players max, and the time frame can span anywhere from an hour or two to several weeks. Though the rules are flexible enough to allow for playing for months, this gets a bit cumbersome when having a small player pool.

Each player gets an ID card ("credentials") and a target name. Unlike the more informal version of the game, players are given specific instructions on how to eliminate their target. It might be luring the target to a location or lying in wait, getting the target to do something, or more. Nailing the target with the squirt gun or "poisoning" their food with salt might be fun but if it's not on the specific method card, it doesn't count. Once you've eliminated your target, your next target becomes whoever your original target was stalking. Gameplay continues until there's only one player left.

I like the way this game refines the elimination process, and I like the smaller, more limited scope. This makes it a good game for family events, fun in the dorms at school or even a company morale booster.

If you've ever played the old elimination game, this will be familiar territory. If you haven't it's a fun introduction. There's reasonably good replayability and there's enough flexibility to either play quickly or draw it out for days and weeks.
text_fidelity_b: TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+

K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy [[VIDEOID:5795137e2a23bd3d76a56d2b9446c889]] If you’re already familiar with K’Nex building sets, this K’NEX THRILL RIDES-REVOLUTION FERRIS WHEEL is a simple, fast build. The Ferris wheel is big, but it doesn’t require a lot of pieces. Also, much of the assembly involves building duplicate parts that combine to make the wheel and its swinging gondolas.

The set is recommended for age 7+, and that sounds reasonable (assuming that an adult provides some initial help with making the connections, and assists with lifting the wheel onto the axle). Each shape of piece is a different color, which detracts from the appearance of the finished Ferris wheel, but makes the construction simpler. There aren’t many “snowflake” connections, which I usually have to puzzle over to get the right orientation. (K’Nex pieces are much harder to work with than LEGO pieces.) The instructions are reasonably clear. This set took me about 5 hours to build (from opening the box to completion, working at a leisurely pace).

Unfortunately, the finished “thrill ride” isn’t very thrilling. Like a full-sized amusement park ride, the Ferris wheel doesn’t do much—it just goes around and around in a circle. Also, it does NOT have a variable speed control—you cannot start, stop, or speed up the wheel gradually (like a real ride). Although the motor has a single speed, it does run in forward and reverse directions. The motor is powered by two AA batteries (not included).

For the Ferris wheel to turn properly, one edge of the inner wheel track must be settled into the groove on the “gear wheel” attached to the motor. You can easily fiddle with the base to adjust things so that the track and groove always make good contact. Because it’s sort of boring and lacks a variable speed control, I rate this K’Nex Ferris Wheel kit at 4 stars (“I like it” on the official Amazon scale).
text_fidelity_b: K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy

CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes I started playing Settlers of Catan when it first came out, many years ago. It has a special place as a gateway game. It brought people who wouldn't normally play anything exotic out of the world of Chutes and Ladders, and into the realm of strategy board games. It's easier to learn than Monopoly, but without the very lengthy period of regret between knowing who will win and actually reaching the foregone conclusion. I largely stopped playing the game about 20 years ago because thanks to Catan, the world of board games exploded into a great variety of games that I consider to be much better. Seeing this fancy set made me want to give it a try again, see what might have changed, and teach the kids.

Unboxing:
The components are visible in the packaging, which is unusual. The outer box is a throwaway, but there is a good sturdy box inside. Everything is packed well enough to avoid shifting and scuffing in transit. There are a few too many components for my taste. It takes quite a while to get everything taken out and put away. I'm fine with that if a game really needs that level of complexity, but I think this one is pushing it. The new three dimensional components make it even more of a chore. I like that the water border clips together securely. In the original, the water spaces tended to slide around, and since the game is about building roads and houses on the cracks, it was destabilizing for everything. Now the board stays together securely, even on carpet.

The new three dimensional tiles are a fun idea, but poorly implemented. Each one needs a convex, translucent, slippery disc on top, but few allowances were made for this in design. They just teeter there and slip around, or sit way off center. I can't support making the number circles translucent. I can't see any positive purpose for it, and it reduces the ability to play with variants that start with some of them face down. After assembling the sea sections, I see that the game board is smaller than I expected. I really like the addition of harbor shapes on the seas to show where the ports should go. The ports themselves are a bit hard to see compared to the old cardboard ones.

The colors chosen for each player are questionable. The parts themselves have a dark wash over them to make the details stand out, but it makes them all dingy. Beige, orange, red, and blue. I guess the blue player can find their pieces, but in dim lighting, the rest look too similar. There's an odd mix of unique things, like the shape of each player's houses, and having things repeat that could have been unique, like all of the forest hexes being identical.

If the instruction book is hard to open, it's because it isn't a book, it's a foldout that folds counterintuitively. There is a quick reference startup guide and another small book with more in-depth details.

It's nice that it comes with card holders, and while it's a chore to get everything back in the box right, at least there's a secure place for everything. The gameplay is as I remember. Simple and engaging enough for most people to be willing to play, and strategic enough to be satisfying. There are games that are both simpler and more strategic out there. Quite a lot of them. In a four player game, anyone who ends up hemmed in by players who chose after them can end up stuck without anywhere to expand. This leads to occasional games like Monopoly, where someone isn't going to be having much fun for an hour. Luck can play a bit too heavily. This was one of the early games that added the excellent mechanic of randomizing the playing field, but the dice too often just end up rolling the same number over and over, which tends to give some players a lot to do and others nothing for several critical turns.

It's strange, but I think I may actually stick with my old plain set. This one feels more fancy and less functional.

The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up Several years ago there was a British series about Robin Hood, and my family and I have been hooked ever since seeing that series. This game seemed like a good fit for my family based on our interests, and so far it has been a good addition to family game night. That said, this game tends to be on the easy side and the replayability isn't great if you want a varying experience.

In a nutshell, this is a basic move-around-the-board game at its heart, though it requires cooperation instead of competition and it relies on a story book to further the game along. Some real time and attention to detail went into the design and it shows.

Though the game does not require following a path without turning to the left or right, it does follow a basic flow and the story book is designed to help guide and direct. That said, it essentially is a map of how to get through each step and it does not vary from game to game so once the game has been played the book could potentially slow down a game instead of moving it along at an interesting pace since previous players will know what to do.

This is certainly not a bad game. It's a good family game and is worth running through as a group. However, for those looking for replayability, this one lacks variety.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up

CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver) This is my first lightsaber in about a decade. The last one I owned what a Force FX by Hasbro; my, how technology has evolved.

This lightsaber is cheaper than the one I purchase, yet has a lot more to offer. While it doesn't have the "expanding" lights (it's sort of like a flashlight), the features it has make up for it. There's only one button, yet it does so much. Initial long press wakes it up or puts it to sleep. While it's on standby, there are button sequences that control music, volume, and sound font.

With the light emitted, the lightsaber has clash functionality, and the ability to change colors. What I love about changing colors is that the colors cycle in a rainbow fashion; there is no predetermined number of colors. See a color you like between cycles? Stop on it and it stays. Pretty nice.

The smooth swing works effectively, but the sound doesn't fade away; instead, there's an abrupt stop. So if you turn the lightsaber one way, the sound follows in synchronization, but immediately stops. It sort of takes away from the effect, but I imagine lightsabers with better smooth-swing functionality have better accuracy.

One day, while charging the lightsaber after a month, the charging sound came on and kept announcing the charging state. I was a little concerned, but left it. Suddenly, the sound was rapid, then silence. I checked the lightsaber and the charging light wasn't on. I tried different outlets, but no fix. Thankfully, the lightsaber is easy to disassemble, so I checked out the battery. It seems fine, but I am awaiting a new one to make sure it's just the battery that was fried.
text_fidelity_b: CVCBSER Flash Smooth Swing FX Dueling Lightsaber with12 Colors and 9 Kinds Mode Sounds Changeable Premium Aluminium Alloy Handle Light Saber Toys (Silver)

Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up This MOONLITE STORYBOOK PROJECTOR (Special Edition Disney Gift Pack, for Ages 1 and Up) is a flawed concept. The projector is difficult to position over the flashlight on my Galaxy S10 phone, unless I turn the phone over and look through the lens at the light. This burns an image into my retina, and is clearly not good for my eyes!

The projector clips onto the phone, and exerts moderate pressure on the screen. I don’t like this, because I worry about cracking the screen.

The projector works with the free “Moonlite” app (available from the App Store or Google Play). You will have to register for an account to use the app. After that, you must activate each set of story reels by entering an activation code--the code is on a small card packed in the box. You tap the “unlock” icon at the top left of the app, and enter the code.

Once you’ve activated the story reel set, you click on the story you want. The app will then display a story for you to read to your child. As you read each page, you advance the reel in the Moonlite projector, to get a new illustration for each page of the story.

The projector shows a focused illustration (focus is adjustable), as long as you are no more than a yard or so away from the surface you are projecting to. You cannot project the picture across a room, or for any great distance, because the phone’s flashlight isn’t bright enough to project for long distances.

The photos that accompany the stories in the Disney set are boring, as are the stories. Kids will no doubt love the Disney characters in the pictures (e.g., Mickey, Minnie, Donald, Goofy), but the story illustrations are repetitious. Also the detail in the illustrations gets lost because the projected images are fairly small.
text_fidelity_b: Moonlite Mini Projector with 5 Classic Winnie The Pooh Stories - A New Way to Read Stories Together - 5 Digital Stories with Light Projector - Winnie The Pooh Toys and Gifts for Kids Ages 1 and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show is a fun way for your little fashion diva to spend some free time. All you do is download the application on your smartphone, tablet, or iPod touch, draw some fashion designs, and then scan them. Your fashion will then show up on an actual fashion model, in 3D, to your child’s delight.

My girls are fashion designers in the making so I knew they would love playing with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show. It takes little effort to get going. You just add the application to your smartphone or tablet, and then have your child start drawing. Once scanned through the application, kids will be able to see their own fashion design on an actual model. This caused squeals of satisfaction from my girls who loved seeing their fashion on screen.

From my children’s perspectives, there is little that isn’t perfect with a toy like this, but as an adult, I can see a few issues. One has already been stated by others who have used the device, but bears repeating: The phone or tablet you use will make a difference. Not all smartphones or tablets are created equally and the colors may look a little off. If you have more than one device and it doesn’t look good on one, then you might want to consider downloading the application to another device. It could make a difference and it’s simple enough to do.

The included accessories with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show are a little limited. The small colored pencils are also somewhat of an obstacle, as they are not good for larger hands. But overall, this is a fun fashion design kit and I cannot imagine a fashion- loving child who wouldn’t fall in love with it.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show

---------------------------------------
* We were finally able to take this tank for a spin. It is indeed super fun. But here are 3 noteworthy things:

1.) It is gigantic, adult supervision is required to make sure kids get in and out of it safely. Never allow them to stand up to get out. Buoyancy can cause them to flip and hit the side of the pool cement. So make sure they simply crawl off the tank slowly and safely, like rolling out of bed. LOL!

It is difficult for little children. So the idea that whoever is in the tank has the advantage is wrong. LOL! In our pool, we all have water guns, and whoever is in the tank becomes the target. LOL! Nevertheless, it's still very fun, and the 5-Star rating is justified.

ORIGINAL REVIEW MAY 4th, 2022:
----------------------------------------

---------------
* Seems like super fun!

* The vinyl feels pretty standard. It did not feel thin or cheap.
* Everything seems to be complete. It even included little repair stickers in case you get holes.

THE BAD:

* Well, we won't exactly know yet until the summer. I got this for the upcoming summer, and I'll be sure to update. My kids can't wait. For now, gotta give it 5-Stars.

B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z Toddlers love to play and they benefit from toys that encourage learning or help in other areas of development. One toy that seems promising in these ways is the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers.

This puzzle has knobs on the pieces, making it easy for toddlers to grab each piece. It helps with coordination, too, as little ones will learn to fit the right shape into the right slot. However, the colors of the pieces are washed out and they really need to be an eye catching primary. Not only would it be more inviting to toddlers and preschoolers but it would provide an opportunity to not only teach numbers and counting, but color recognition too while playing.

Another issue with the pieces is that the details are lacking. If you are going to add detail make it something a child can recognize. But probably the most shocking oversight is the shapes and numbers that they are supposed to match. There is an octagon, for example, that represents the number 7, a five- pointed star that is used for the number 8, and so on. Why would you do this? The octagon should be the number 8 and the star should match with number 5. This is an oversight that someone should have caught.

Other issues I have are with the puzzle holes- they are a little too big and this would be hard to travel anywhere with. I do like that the numbers are nice and big and easy to see and that the knobs are big and tall enough for tiny fingers to grasp. While I haven’t seen it happen yet I do worry because, since they are very much like thumbtacks, they may come loose and eventually get lost. The pieces don’t hold in place as well as I would like.

Toddler toys that help kids learn are nice and while the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers does help with coordination and other skills, it lacks in other areas. The oversight with the numbers and shapes not matching is a big one and I have other issues, too. So, when I think of everything as a whole, this toy gets a thumbs down from me.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z

The irregularly shaped pieces, the use of colors in small areas across the entire puzzle, and the confusing curved lines in the design add greatly to the difficulty.

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book I never really thought I would be calling any toy a godsend, but the Crayola Glow Book has done something for my ten-year-old son that none of his school teachers (and certainly not his art teacher) has been able to do. I've tried, too. I've tried asking, showing, cajoling, ordering, limiting privileges, exaggerated sighing, and using his full name, but my child's penmanship is abysmal and his art skills mostly stink.

The reason for this is relatively straightforward: in my family, kids develop their fine motor skills later than most kids do. My parents and teachers made me work at it, but I at least was getting a lot of practice all the time. My child goes to a school where he gets to type a lot of his assignments. He's learned a lot in art about color and perspective and design, but he gets extremely frustrated trying to execute what's in his head, so he stopped enjoying drawing and painting pretty much as soon as he hit kindergarten.

When I ordered this, I thought it was going to turn out to be just a gimmicky gadgety thing he'd use once and then I'd get to use it to leave notes my husband would have to work to ignore, but my son loves it. He can write, draw, erase, illuminate, and animate without having to commit anything to paper or to critical eyes (except his own). Because the illustration plates are layered, if he's happy with one part but not another, he can re-do the one without having to worry about smudging or wrecking the other. As a result, he is spending time using his fine motor skills, they are improving, and he is much happier with the work he is doing.

I gave this five stars for fun, based on his recommendation. I rate it five stars for educational value and five stars overall for how much help it has been in an area in which my child needed some help. I gave it four stars for durability. It feels a little flimsy, but it's holding up well so far.

UPDATE: When you exhaust the markers that come with this, you can use dry erase markers on it. They're actually a little bit easier to see and work with, they come in tons of colors, and they clean right up.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

Lulu Jr. My Comic Book - Create Your Own Comic This kit made my daughter so excited she literally ran out to the delivery man to get it squealing. She loves ANYTHING art related.

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
The kit comes in a nice box which is not too big, so it is easy to store while working on the comic.

The kit has a decent booklet inside which covers the following:
-Characters (ideas for who to draw)
-Settings (locations)
-Panels (how to draw and use them)
-Words (balloons, types of words and sounds)
-Styles of topics (flavor of the book)
-Art Style (realistic, cartoony, stick figures, etc)
-Character personality (giving depth to the character by quirks)
-Props to make the story interesting
-Panels and perspective
-Dialogue and sound effects
-Icons that are used to translate ideas, heat, etc
-Idea starters (great boxes with beginning sentences to motivate and inspire)
-Practice pages

There is a sheet which gives the specs for how the book will be printed and what not to use and what to use on the comic for printing. There is a series of design sheets that will be submitted to the publisher. A postage paid envelope is included for submitting the finished comic.

The kit also comes with markers, pencil, eraser, sharpener and a pen.

OVERALL COMMENTS
I think that this kit is a great inspiration for anyone who wants to make a comic. The instructional manual has great ideas to springboard from. My daughter is having some difficulty narrowing down her final ideas, but she has spent a lot of time considering and thinking of what to make her final comic like. This is a great gift and also a great addition to homeschool or art classes if you have a child who loves to draw and who especially likes comic books.

I am under a time constraint to publish this review, so I will update it when my daughter finishes her final product, submits it to the company, and receives the final comic back. At the time of this review, I am giving it five stars, but will adjust if I find that the final submission process warrants it.

It's her first light-up Fingerling but most of it's movements/interactions are basically the same as her others, just sounds a little different (cat/panther sounds vs. monkeys, sloths, etc).

Allec is very cute! She comes with a mini Fingerling- her cub Ronni, which is solid plastic and does not interact in any type of way- but you can place it on a pencil or snuggle her between Allec's arms and tummy.

- Burps and giggles when you hold her upside down and press your palm down her forehead for a few seconds. Hair lights up green and blue.

- Makes silly reactions when hanging upside down. Hair lights up red, yellow and blue

- She gets bored and makes sounds. Hair lights up blue, green, teal.

- Responds in different ways when you pet her head. Hair lights up all of the different colors.

A couple things to note: Her glitter doesn't shed. She doesn't require other separate accessories to enjoy.

text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do Art 3D Gel Painting Let me start off by admitting that the kids DID have fun playing with it. That's why it deserves at least 3 stars. But it is surprisingly messy for a product that claims to be for kids. They had a really hard time washing it off their hands, and there's a big warning on the package (which we didn't notice until after opening it) that says it may stain fabrics. The paint really easily gets everywhere- we found more of it the day after cleaning it up that we didn't even notice. On that note, the 3D aspect of it is kind of gimmicky at best. You can't really make a three dimensional structure, at most you can make little mountain dollops (as pictured) which take forever to dry. As in, you might need to keep it in a safe place for a couple of days before anyone can touch it. To be fair, they call it "fluffy", which it is. But the marketing would have you believe it can be somehow used to create 3D depth sort of like play-doh, which isn't true. Actually, I think Play-doh would probably have been a better project than this. Easier to clean up, can mix colors and make shapes, and dries into solid 3D shapes. But then again you can't use that to paint a picture as well, which this sort of does. So I guess this is sort of a product in between paint and play-doh. Not really what we were expecting.
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell Do Art 3D Gel Painting

Ontel Magic Tracks Police Chase Glow in The Dark Racetrack Set with 10 Feet of Speedway OK, first off - we really love Magic/Neo/Twister Tracks. We have a number of different sets. Recently we grabbed the one with the single car and remote, along with the Rocket Racers and an off brand, dinosaur-themed set. All of which were excellent! This however, has a major flaw.

The jump ramp seems like an afterthought. It looks nothing like the picture on the box. It's like the box graphics were designed before the physical product. Even worse, its the connection to the track makes zero sense, and the instructions are laughable to say the lease. Oddly enough, the ramp is able to move back and forth like a see-saw, yet, it's not meant to do that! It's a ramp - and it's supposed to let the truck fly off and onto the lower track. Here's the kicker: one side of the ramp is blocked, like a dead end, so the only way we got this to work was to lay the proceeding track over it so it the truck wouldn't be stopped. It's like the manufacture designed this ramp piece wrong. Between that, and the see saw spring built in, my bet is, this was meant to originally do something else, but it failed, so they left it that way and simply called it a jump ramp. At 29.95, that's a disgrace. This is the only set we sent back. Most of the high ratings you see are for the other themes (firetruck, police set, etc..), so proceed with caution.
text_fidelity_b: Ontel Magic Tracks Police Chase Glow in The Dark Racetrack Set with 10 Feet of Speedway

text_fidelity_a:
Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces THE GOOD:
--------------
* Perfectly priced toy for the quality you're getting.
* Collectible.
* Like Rock-Em Sockem, but with electronics, and the figures will split when getting knocked out.
* This version come with an arena, but you can fight without it if you wish.
* Two warriors included to get you started.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Nothing I can think of. The price is just right for what you're getting. I don't recall an actual arcade game in the past called Akedo. It seems this toy is simply inspired by all the classic arcade fighting games such as Street Fighter, Fatal Fury, Tekken, etc. It will keep your children occupied for awhile and away from tablets.

One more thing, the two default figures that's already installed in the arena have clear bands wrapped around them. We saw the vertical bands on their bodies and cut them off. But when we battled, we still couldn't split each other. My son realize there are more tiny bands in the neck that needs to be cut. So if you're playing for awhile, and you can't knock anybody out, check to see if rubber bands are still holding their bodies tight. You can manually check... you are free of bands when you can pop their heads back and split their bodies. If you can't do that, it probably means there are some bands you still need to cut off.

5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Ultimate Battle Arena Action Figure, 3 Pieces

Hot Wheels Set of 15 Toy Cars or Trucks, 3 Themed 5-Packs of 1:64 Scale Die-Cast Vehicles (Styles May Vary) When I was a kid I used to love Hot Wheels cars and I had a nice collection of them. These little cars have been around for a long time and they have changed some but they're still a lot of fun, even for adults. I selected this set not so much for playing but for photography and so far I am pleased with them.

These are a set of three themed packs of 5 cars each. The cars are reasonably well made (though there is a lot more plastic than when I used to collect these as a kid) and they seem to be painted cleanly as well. They roll straight right ouf the package too. For someone interested in little cars like these, this is a nice set to get started or to rapidly expand a collection.

The one car in the set that I do not light is the skateboarder. I would rather have had another little truck or a rally car or something. Even a beat-up old truck with primer would have been more fun for me, but I digress.

Price-wise these are quire reasonable. As I write this, the set is about $32, and that translates to just over $2/car. When comparing individual cars priced against this collection it's clear this is a decent value.

I like these and they serve my purpose quite well. These seem to be made well and they're priced right. If you want to start a collection or want to expand one quickly, this is a good collection.

Adora Baby Bath Toy Llama-Corn, 13 inch Bath Time Doll with QuickDri Body My four-year-old granddaughter has been very pleased with every Adora doll I have given her so far, including this one. She likes cuddling this baby doll and carrying it around and, of course, wanted to give it a whirl using it in the tub. Based on that experience, I've listed below some pros and cons of the doll that have been more of an issue for the adults in my granddaughter's life than for her. In other words, they did not seem to lessen her appreciation of the doll but can make caring for the doll a real hassle for adult caretakers of very young owners of this doll.

Pros:

1. This is a very cute doll. It has a sweet face with lifelike detailing of its features and real eyelashes (versus ones that are painted on). The plastic used for the head, arms, legs, hands, and feet is not hard and unyielding but appealingly soft and pliable. The hair is painted, raised plastic rather than rooted hair since this doll is meant to be immersed in water.

2. The doll can suck its thumb, and its eyes open and close.

3. The doll is wearing a non-removable swimsuit and an adorable, removable, terrycloth robe whose hood is the head of a baby unicorn. It also comes with a monogrammed towel.

4. The doll is machine washable in cold water on delicate cycle, but I'm not sure why anybody would want to put a doll in the washing machine. It seems more sensible to take a far less aggressive approach by simply using a damp washcloth to wipe it down. Note that you absolutely cannot put this doll in the dryer.

Cons:

1. The body of this doll seems to have stuffing made of some kind of beads, possibly Styrofoam pellets, similar to what is found in beanbag chairs. Whatever it is that is inside the body, it absorbs water like a sponge, making it very difficult to get all of the accumulated bath or pool water out of the doll. As a result, it can take up to 24 hours for the doll to dry fully. And there's a real risk that the inside of the doll will potentially, perpetually retain enough dampness that it becomes a breeding ground for mold.

2. As seems to be a company policy for all Adora dolls (at least for the four or five Adora dolls I've purchased), this doll has a fake sent of baby powder that's quite unpleasant for anyone sensitive to chemicals. I seem to be the only one in my immediate and extended family with this problem so, fortunately, it did not bother my granddaughter or her parents.

3. The doll's thumb does not fit securely into its mouth, and it pops out far too easily.

4. This doll seems priced too high for what it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Adora Baby Bath Toy Llama-Corn, 13 inch Bath Time Doll with QuickDri Body

text_fidelity_a: 2 Pairs Genuine DJI 9450 Self-tightening Propellers for Phantom 3 Pro, Adv (Gold Stripes) These are exact replacement parts for the DJI Phantom 3 drones. The gold tips on the blades are a nice touch, to match the other gold trim on the P3P. This type of blade also fits many other quadcopters that use the same type screw on propeller shaft, replacing the slip on props and lock nuts, which often come off during flight, causing a lot of crashes, damage and even lost quads. My advice is always use the self tightening props. But, avoid those with metal hubs. The metal hubs will either lock on too tight or not tight enough. Composite hubs, like these, are always best.

Grandpa Beck's Games The Bears and The Bees | A Delightfully Strategic Tile Laying Game Ideal for Kids, Teens, & Adults | from The Creators of Cover Your Assets & Skull King, 2-5 Players 7+ I love this game! I think I have every Grandpa Becks game, starting with Cover Your Assets and this and Cover Your Assets is one of my favorite games to play. Birds and Bees is a pretty quick game to learn and you can play a complete game in twenty to thirty minutes.

I think it's fun to match the colors and patterns . I'm slightly color blind - ok- a lot color blind, and my family loves to tease me as I have a hard time telling the difference between the red and purple colors on the cards. So it's become a standing joke, if I put a card down that is red or purple the family makes sure I'm not "cheating". I just laugh, Darn when my color doesn't work!

The other great thing about this card game is that anyone can play it. We have a family member that has autism and he is actually really good at this game, has figured out the strategy, what cards to get rid of immediately, aka the Bear and the flowers and he regularly beats us. I highly recommend this game. A lot of fun for your family.
